opening.argument: The clearest character of this material is a science Q&A: named experts answer questions submitted through Twitter, with the discussion focused on topics such as memory and scientific research. One speaker expressly says, "Today, I'm gonna answer some of your questions on Twitter," while another explains that research on eliminating memories remains limited to mice. The displayed questions likewise concern memory and tractor beams, reinforcing an educational and operational discussion rather than a financial opportunity. No evidence establishes a request for payment or private information. Any urgent cure-related wording is insufficient to establish solicitation because the available speech is garbled and does not clarify who made the statement or whether it was quoted, reported, or criticized.

citations.quote: Bill Nye, Neil DeGrasse Tyson, doctor turned actor Ken Jeong, science fiction director James Cameron, former NASA astronaut Scott Kelly and neuroscientist Anil Seth answer the most interesting science questions from Twitter.
Today, I'm gonna answer some of your questions on Twitter.
We're not quite there yet, but there's some interesting work in just with mice at the moment that shows it is possible to eliminate certain memories from mice.
